standard_prerequisites.name: Henselization and completion of a Noetherian local ring, and their agreement
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the reduction that lets A be assumed henselian.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient-by-idempotent lemma for a quotient of an adic completion killing a square-zero annihilated ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite type A-algebra C whose completion is A-hat/J.

standard_prerequisites.name: The structure of unramified ring maps as quotients of etale algebras, and the rigidity of etale algebras over a henselian local ring with trivial residue extension
standard_prerequisites.use: Forces B = A after localization and hence C = A/I.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness and flatness of the completion map
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives J = IA-hat and I = J cap A, which turn the containment into the radical statement.

core_obligations: Use that A and A^h have the same completion to reduce to the case where A is henselian (proof lines 32109-32110).

Apply the quotient-by-idempotent lemma to A-hat -> A-hat/J with J = Ker(A-hat -> (A-hat)_q); for this, deduce from dim((A-hat)_q) = 0 that q^n is contained in J for some n, hence J/J^2 is annihilated by q^n (proof lines 32111-32115).

Show that a power of m annihilates J/J^2: use (J/J^2)_q = 0 because J_q = 0, conclude that m is the only associated prime of J/J^2, and apply the lemma to get A-hat/J = C-hat for some finite type A-algebra C (proof lines 32116-32121).
Use that C/mC = A/m to see that m_C = mC is a maximal ideal and that A -> C is unramified at m_C (proof lines 32124-32127).

After a principal localization, realize C as a quotient of an etale A-algebra B using the structure proposition for unramified maps, and conclude B = A after a localization because the residue field extension of A -> C_{m_C} is trivial and A is henselian; hence C = A/I for some ideal I (proof lines 32128-32134).

Conclude J = IA-hat by exactness of completion in this situation and I = J cap A by flatness of A -> A-hat; with q^n contained in J contained in q, obtain that p = q cap A satisfies p^n contained in I contained in p, and hence sqrt(p A-hat) = q (proof lines 32134-32141).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) with henselization A^h and a minimal prime q of the completion A-hat with dim(A-hat/q) = 1, and asserts the existence of a minimal prime q^h of A^h with q = sqrt(q^h A-hat) (source lines 32099-32106). The proof is a two-stage descent. Since A and A^h have the same completion, one may assume A is henselian; then one applies the quotient-by-idempotent lemma to the surjection A-hat -> A-hat/J with J = Ker(A-hat -> (A-hat)_q), which requires proving that a power of m annihilates J/J^2: the proof obtains q^n contained in J because dim((A-hat)_q) = 0, chooses a power of m annihilating J/J^2 using that (J/J^2)_q = 0 and that m is the only associated prime of J/J^2, and concludes that A-hat/J is the completion of a finite type A-algebra C (proof lines 32109-32121). The second stage identifies C: since C/mC = A/m, the ideal m_C = mC is maximal and A -> C is unramified there; after a principal localization C is a quotient of an etale A-algebra B by the structure proposition for unramified maps, and because the residue field extension of A -> C_{m_C} is trivial and A is henselian one gets B = A after a localization, so C = A/I for some ideal I (proof lines 32124-32134). Finally the proof shows J = IA-hat by exactness of completion in this situation and I = J cap A by flatness of A -> A-hat, so with q^n contained in J contained in q one gets p = q cap A satisfying p^n contained in I contained in p, and hence sqrt(p A-hat) = q (proof lines 32134-32141). The non-routine content is the two-step annihilation of J/J^2 that makes the quotient lemma applicable, and the henselian rigidity that forces the unramified algebra to be A itself.
